items.title: 3 reasons Elden Ring gamers will love Phantom Blade Zero, and 3 reasons they won't
items.summary: It's going to be a blast either way...
items.content:
Phantom Blade Zero is going to cater massively to the soulsborne/Elden Ring crowd. Here's what you need to know...

Phantom Blade Zero launches later this month, and it’s going to be a pretty big deal.

The kung-fu-punk action-adventure game is like John Wick with more martial arts, and soulslike fans are going to love it.

While it’s not part of the soulslike genre, it does borrow quite a few elements from it. After going hands-on with the game for over six hours , I can confidently say it executes them flawlessly, and I’m adamant that FromSoftware fans are going to love it…mostly.

Below are three reasons I think you’ll get a kick out of Phantom Blade Zero if you’re into games like Elden Ring , and three that might leave you on the fence. Regardless, I’d encourage you to try the game for yourself when it launches on October 29.

This is a given. During my hands-on preview, I fought more bosses than expected, and with the sole exception of one, they were all certified bangers.

One boss in particular shone above all the rest, and even surpasses a similar fight found in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree

READ NEXT: Phantom Blade Zero does an Elden Ring boss leagues better than FromSoftware

Elden Ring broke the mold with its character builds, as unlike previous FromSoftware games, you had the opportunity to change your stats with a finite supply of Larval Tears.

While I’m glad this was added, Phantom Blade Zero does it better. Soul’s upgrades don’t matter as much as the weapon upgrades. The power of your build lies in your weapons.

Several weapons were unlocked for my preview, and what I loved most was how you could upgrade one as much as you want, then reverse it. You’d get all of your upgrade materials back, ready to be distributed into weapons you want to use instead.

It just made everything so simple, which is perfect for those who want to try out several different approaches to combat.

Something that’s rarely been talked about regarding Phantom Blade Zero is the awesome 66 Days mode you’ll unlock after beating the main story.

This is where the soulslike crowd should be looking if they want a real challenge, as it turns Soul’s 66 days to live into an actual game mechanic, rather than a narrative device.

items.title: PlayStation Plus' new Elden Ring rival tackles my biggest issue with FromSoftware's work
items.summary: Variety is the spice of life, they say ✨
items.content:
The PlayStation Plus October bumper drop adds a soulsgame I'd highly recommend to those who find FromSoftware's work a bit too tedious.

PlayStation Plus’ October bumper drop includes some excellent games for your PlayStation Plus Extra subscription, but it's the Premium offering that’s caught our eye.

To be more specific PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers get access to one of my new favourite soulslikes, one I’d even hold above some FromSoftware titles.

That may sound like sacrilege to some, but hear me out. Since my early teen years I’ve been a massive fan of FromSoftware, with Dark Souls being one of my favourite games ever made. In fact it’s my Game of the Year, every year .

However, Mortal Shell II seriously impressed me, so I’m thrilled that more people get to experience it through PlayStation Plus Premium. On October 20 a free trial will launch.

It’s tough to make a soulslike game feel like anything but a half-hearted attempt to ride FromSoftware’s coattails, though many games like Lies of P have done a good job of being unique.

Mortal Shell II joins that exclusive club with its core mechanic, ‘shells’. Rather than creating one character and slowly creating a build as time goes on, Mortal Shell II gives you flexibility. The shells are found throughout the world and each one has its own stats, weapons and more.

You can freely switch between them, which tackles one of the few gripes I have with FromSoftware games. When I play soulslikes I often find myself naturally gravitating towards a strength-build. It’s the “big stick go bonk” caveman approach a lot of players find themselves slipping into and while it is good fun, by the end of my playthrough I wish I’d done things differently.

Elden Ring thankfully breaks tradition and lets you change your build with Larval Tears, though there’s a finite supply so you can’t get too crazy with it. It also doesn’t solve another problem; weapons. To fully change your build in Elden Ring you need to alter your stats, find an upgrade new weapons to compliment your build, and of course acquire new drip to match your new personality.

Mortal Shell II trims the fat, and while it doesn’t make the game easier by any means it does make it more engaging.

After recently going hands-on with Phantom Blade Zero I was thoroughly impressed with the way it’s handling its weapon upgrades, and the same theory is being applied in Mortal Shell II; players need variety.

READ NEXT: 6 reasons why Phantom Blade Zero will be the best action game of all-time

FromSoftware’s unlikely to adopt this style of gameplay in its future games and to be honest I hope it doesn’t, but it is something other soulslikes should take note of.

We shouldn’t need to start entirely new playthroughs just to try something new. It should be baked into the gameplay in one way or another.

items.title: Which sci-fi film will bring Zendaya and Alex Garland together?
items.summary: Screenwriter and director Alex Garland, at the helm of the film adaptation of Elden Ring, is preparing a new sci-fi project starring Zendaya.
items.content:
British screenwriter and director Alex Garland ( Ex Machina , Civil War ) is at the helm of the film adaptation of Elden Ring , the video game co-created by George R.R. Martin, the mastermind behind the Game of Thrones saga. In 2027, he will then turn his attention to a sci-fi project starring Zendaya.

It has been A24 ’s boldest gamble so far. The American independent studio known for Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022), Civil War (2024) and Marty Supreme (2026) is investing more than $100 million in the adaptation of Elden Ring . This dark fantasy video game was developed by FromSoftware ( Dark Souls ) under the direction of Hidetaka Miyazaki and based on the mythology imagined by George R.R. Martin , author of the cult literary saga Game of Throne s. A24’s previous budget record was held by Marty Supreme (2026), starring Timothée Chalamet , with $70 million.

Released in 2022, the game has sold more than 30 million copies and won over 400 Game of the Year awards. In a world known as the Lands Between, the Elden Ring, the source of all order, has been shattered by the descendants of Queen Marika, corrupted demigods who divided its fragments among themselves and plunged the kingdom into chaos. Players take on the role of a Tarnished, an exile summoned back to journey across this ravaged land, confront the demigods and restore the Ring in order to become the new Elden Lord…

Cailee Spaeny for the Los Angeles premiere Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery , at the Academy of Motion Pictures on November 17th, 2025. © JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images. Cailee Spaeny, star of Alex Garland’s new feature The adaptation was only made possible thanks to Alex Garland’s determination. The British filmmaker behind Ex Machina (2014), Annihilation (2018) and Civil War (2024) wrote a 160-page screenplay accompanied by 40 pages of visuals, before travelling to Japan to pitch the project directly to Hidetaka Miyazaki , who gave him his blessing.

As for the cast, Kit Connor , who rose to fame in the series Heartstopper and worked with Alex Garland in Warfare (2025), will take on the lead role. He will be joined by Ben Whishaw ( Black Doves ) and Cailee Spaeny ( Priscilla , Alien: Romulus ), who previously worked with Alex Garland on Civil War . Alongside them are Tom Burke ( Furiosa ), Nick Offerman ( The Last of Us ), Havana Rose Liu ( Bottoms ), Sonoya Mizuno ( Ex Machina ) and Jonathan Pryce ( The Crown ).

Zendaya at the Louis Vuitton Spring/Summer 2027 show in Paris. © Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images pour Louis Vuitton. A sci-fi film starring Zendaya The filming of Elden Ring started in April 2026 in the United Kingdom, particularly in Scotland, with additional sequences shot in Iceland last summer. Two ideal locations for bringing the game’s medieval dark fantasy universe to the screen, with its colossal Gothic architecture and Lovecraftian creatures lurking in bleak, terrifying landscapes.

But Alex Garland is already setting another project in motion, this time starring Zendaya . It will be a sci-fi film produced by A24. While filming is scheduled for 2027, the feature has no official title or synopsis yet. The project will allow the actress to return to a genre (science fiction) she knows well thanks to the Dune saga.

Elden Ring (2028) by Alex Garland does not have a release date yet. Alex Garland’s sci-fi film starring Zendaya does not have a title or release date yet.

items.title: Elden Ring Shadow Of The Erdtree Finally Gets A Discount, And Your NG+ Save Isn’t Ready
Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

items.title: Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different
items.content:

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nodusfall has been Gamescom's biggest surprise: a new co-op action romp from the masters of gacha, HoYoverse, which seemingly does away with so much of what we all associate with the developer.

HoYoverse's games are normally vibrant anime affairs full of waifus and himbos waiting to be collected by thirsty players. Even as the genres and systems change from game to game, the studio has a distinct style and design philosophy—one that's been incredibly successful.

Instead of resting on its laurels, however, HoYoverse is taking a big swing with Nodusfall. One of the most fundamental changes is that characters are not obtained through random draws . This is not your typical gacha game. Indeed, HoYoverse hasn't confirmed any gacha mechanics yet—though we do know that cosmetic monetisation is being considered.

When it was first unveiled during Gamescom's Opening Night Live, the immediate comparisons being bandied around were Elden Ring and Monster Hunter, both of which are fair comparisons but which don't really tell the whole story. That they are inspirations seems undeniable, but Nodusfall is absolutely doing its own thing here.

First of all: Nodusfall is not remotely a soulslike. What it has in common with Elden Ring, then, is largely aesthetic and vibes. As HoYoverse describes it, the world of Nodusfall is one where "divine authority has crumbled and order has collapsed". It's simultaneously bleak and beautiful.

HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall Nodusfall First Reveal Trailer: "Wield Divinity, Sever the Dreadnodus" - YouTube Watch On Monster Hunter is a closer relative. Solo adventurers and groups can select contracts, and then go out into the world to hunt down big beasties. These are lengthy, elaborate fights with multiple phases, taking place in spacious outdoor areas. So yeah, this all felt immediately evocative of Monster Hunter. But the similarities largely end there.

My four-player crew started off in a hub area, where we could select and customise our characters—one of which had two classes, while the rest had one. I opted for a serious looking lad with a big sword, serving as the group's tank. So you're not just creating a customisable blank slate who is defined by whatever weapon they happen to be holding.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Each character has dramatically different combat styles and unique mechanics, so while I was going to spend the next 30 minutes blocking damage with my huge weapon and sticking to foes like angry velcro, another member of the party was going to spend that same time hanging back and healing my reckless ass. Nodusfall isn't an RPG, but it does have an RPG's role-based classes.

Our HoYoverse babysitter led us to our battles—three boss-style scraps with an escalating level of challenge, culminating in a massive brawl against a huge dragon and its giant, heavily-armoured rider. There wasn't much time for faffing in the open area, though I did clock other creatures ambling around—but we were here for larger prey.

It's more aggressive and spammy than Monster Hunter, but some precision is still required.

Even as a slow tank, I was surprisingly agile. Unless you've volunteered for healer duty, Nodusfall is a brisk, relentless kind of action game, where you'll be stringing together impressively flashy combos as you keep an eye on your skill cooldowns. And all the while, you'll feel like a human shaped missile, always launching yourself at whatever creature is in your sights.

I became rather fond of the clash mechanic, where you charge up a strong attack, and release it right as the monster is about to hit you, countering the attack. It helps that I looked stylish doing it, with my already massive sword growing, transforming into a magical, glowing WMD.

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: Is Elden Ring the best of the Souls series?
items.summary: Is Elden Ring the best Soulslike game ever made? Explore how FromSoftware reinvented the genre with open-world freedom, epic boss fights, and unmatched player choice.
items.content:
For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games and inspired players of all ages.

Let’s take a look at how ELDEN RING has elevated and perfected the original Souls series formula and explore if ELDEN RING could be the best of the entire Souls series.

The majority of the games were designed by Hidetaka Miyazaki to give players the experience of exploring dark and majestic fantasy worlds full of danger.

There’s also a strong focus on difficulty, world structure, boss fights, and player builds.

The difficulty of the Souls series stems from their combat design. They emphasize deliberate attack and evasion in response to enemy movement, which tends to be quick, fierce, and punishing for players who find themselves out of position at the wrong moment. Players need to carefully observe and learn their foes’ patterns, then react to exploit certain specific attack openings without leaving themselves open as well.

This type of careful, evasive gameplay mimics the danger and strategy of real hand-to-hand combat and the high stakes keeps the tension and excitement rising in each fight. It’s not as simple as playing out a power fantasy where enemies easily fall to repeated mindless button mashing. For most players, this difficulty means that the feeling of mastering Souls series combat is a rush of pure accomplishment.

In the earlier Souls series games , levels are massive, interconnected linear paths. These paths often have several branching paths that reward exploration and puzzle solving, but are limited in terms of true open field exploration, as it’s necessary to follow a specific set order of levels, usually connected by a hub area where players can regroup, level up and open new paths, to progress throughout the game.

In the best Souls series games , carefully studying the environment and enemy behavior can lead to hidden areas or items, a particular strength of the Dark Souls series, and many players consider level design that rewards careful exploration to be a critical feature of Dark Souls-like games .

Throughout the Souls series , boss battles are powerful climatic moments that put a player’s abilities to the test. In the Dark Souls series , specifically, from the Asylum Demon to Slave Knight Gael , the Dark Souls bosses are encounters that inspire fear, awe, pity, and wonder.

Bosses also act as progression gates that require a certain level of fluency with the game’s combat system before the player can continue to explore. Once a player reaches a boss gate, they must either muster the skill to defeat that boss, or continue to practice and grind on earlier enemies.

Unlike the average enemy that players must face in a limited area not much wider than a typical hallway, bosses are frequently found in massive arenas. Bosses in the Souls series also tend to have enhanced abilities that require the player to adapt to attacks that cover huge areas or have extended reach. This ferocity and enlarged battlefield gives the designers space to create exciting, multi-phase duels that are unforgettably intense.

These boss fights also act as a check on the player’s build. No matter which weapons or elements a player prefers, massive and powerful bosses require adaptation.

Experienced players understand how each type of stat affects their damage output and they use all of the gear at their disposal to create a move set that fits their style and is powerful enough to take down bosses.

items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
